name: Acme External Exposure Review
summary: This review looked at what an outsider can learn about Acme Ltd from public sources only. It found exposed credentials in public breach data, a leaked access key in a public code repository and weak email authentication. No system was accessed.
methodology: Sources: public DNS and certificate transparency records, public code hosting search, breach notification services, company website and professional networking pages. All collection was passive. Each finding is graded for source reliability (A-F) and information credibility (1-6).

scope.rules_of_engagement: No denial-of-service. Business hours only. No real customer data.

findings.title: Secrets exposed in a public code repository
findings.description: A cloud access key belonging to Acme was committed to a public repository and remained in the commit history.
findings.impact: Anyone could use the key to reach the cloud account until it is revoked.
findings.remediation: Revoke and rotate the exposed secrets, remove them from history, and add secret scanning to the development workflow.
sources: Public code hosting repository, commit from 2026-08-14 (collected 2026-10-09)

findings.title: Organisation credentials found in public breach data
findings.description: 12 e-mail addresses on the acme.test domain appear in a public breach collection together with passwords.
findings.impact: Reused passwords may let attackers sign in to company services.
findings.remediation: Force password resets for affected accounts, enforce multi-factor authentication and monitor breach notifications.

findings.title: Weak or missing email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC)
findings.description: The domain publishes an SPF record but no DMARC policy, so spoofed e-mail is not rejected.
findings.impact: Attackers may be able to send spoofed email that appears to come from the organisation.
findings.remediation: Publish SPF and DKIM records and move DMARC to an enforcing policy after monitoring.

findings.title: Forgotten or unmonitored subdomains
findings.description: old-portal.acme.test appears in certificate transparency logs and its web page has not changed since 2023.
findings.impact: Neglected hosts widen the attack surface and can be taken over if DNS records dangle.
findings.remediation: Maintain an asset inventory, remove stale DNS records and retire unused hosts.

findings.title: Look-alike domains registered
findings.description: acme-corp.example was registered by a third party two weeks ago and resolves to a parked page.
findings.impact: Look-alike domains can be used for phishing or brand abuse.
findings.remediation: Monitor new registrations, consider defensive registrations and use takedown procedures where abuse is confirmed.

findings.title: Employee information publicly discoverable
findings.description: Staff names and job titles for the finance team are listed on professional networking sites.
findings.impact: The information can support targeted phishing and social engineering.
findings.remediation: Review what staff and the company publish, provide awareness training and apply email filtering.

objectives: Identify internet-facing assets that Acme may not be tracking
Find publicly exposed credentials or secrets
Assess how easily staff can be targeted by social engineering

timeline.title: Leaked key found
timeline.detail: Access key in a public repository commit

timeline.title: Breach exposure confirmed
timeline.detail: 12 staff e-mail addresses in a public breach collection

entities.name: acme-corp.example
entities.notes: Look-alike registered by a third party

recommendations: Treat exposed secrets as compromised: rotate them first, then investigate. Set up continuous monitoring for new subdomains and breach exposures.
